learning_objective: 🎯 Let us learn how to compare things using positive, comparative, and superlative adjectives!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: We use the positive degree when we just describe one thing without comparing it to anything else. Example: Rohan is a tall boy.
When comparing two things, we usually add '-er' to the adjective and use the word 'than'. Example: Rohan is taller than Amit.
When comparing three or more things, we add '-est' and always put 'the' before it. Example: Rohan is the tallest boy in the class!
Some words change completely instead of using -er or -est! Example: Good becomes Better, and then Best. Bad becomes Worse, and then Worst!

fun_activity.title: ⚖️ Family Height Line-Up
fun_activity.instructions: Stand next to your family members. Point and say who is tall (Positive), who is taller (Comparative), and who is the tallest (Superlative)!

quick_recap: ⭐ Positive degree describes one single noun.
⭐ Superlative degree (-est) compares three or more things.
⭐ Irregular adjectives like 'Good' and 'Bad' have their own special spelling rules.
